# Intake Brief: Audit freshness invalidates only on this work item's own data change

## Problem statement

The audit freshness gate invalidates a stored audit when ANY of its content-fingerprint components change: git HEAD sha, work-item description hash, Key Files list, and working-tree state (`git status --porcelain` + `git diff --name-only HEAD`). Because the fingerprint includes the **whole-repo** git HEAD sha and working-tree state, a commit to dev from an *unrelated* work item (or any uncommitted/untracked file change) invalidates every stored audit in the worklog and re-triggers the full audit pipeline — even though the audited item itself never changed.

**Observed failure (SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0):** the item was audited "Ready to close: Yes" at HEAD `310773d5`. Afterward, an unrelated work item (SA-0MSQ026T3009QY2L) merged `aaabdede` to dev. The content fingerprint changed (verified: stored `58947e06…` matches recomputation at `310773d5` but not at `aaabdede`), so the audit went stale, the re-audit ran, and it blocked on the pre-flight full-suite cache gate — leaving a verified "Ready to close: Yes" item stuck in review.

## Users

- Audit operators / automated dispatchers relying on `audit_runner.py` freshness short-circuit (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT) to skip re-audits of unchanged items.

**User story:** "As an audit operator, I want a stored audit to remain valid unless THIS work item's own data changes, so unrelated repository activity doesn't invalidate my audits."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_content_fingerprint` is computed from the **work item's own data only** — the work item's description (which contains the ACs and the Key Files section) plus its title. The **git HEAD sha and working-tree-state components are removed** from the fingerprint entirely (no git calls in the computation).
2. A git HEAD move caused by ANY other work item's commit does **not** invalidate a stored audit of an item whose own data is unchanged. Regression test: fingerprint is stable when only the HEAD sha differs (item data identical).
3. Uncommitted and untracked working-tree changes do **not** invalidate a stored audit. Regression test: fingerprint is stable across `git status --porcelain` / `git diff --name-only HEAD` differences.
4. A change to this item's own data (title / description / ACs / Key Files section) after the audit **does** invalidate and re-runs the pipeline (existing description/key-files fingerprint tests remain green).
5. Comments, status/stage/priority/assignee changes, and sortIndex changes do **not** invalidate (they move `updatedAt` but are not audited content).
6. **Migration of legacy v1 reports:** reports persisted before this change carry fingerprints computed with the git-inclusive formula that cannot be recomputed. Version the fingerprint line (e.g. `Audit content fingerprint (v2): <hash>`) so legacy lines are distinguishable; legacy reports fall back to the existing time-gate floor (auditedAt vs updatedAt + `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS`) — **no silent mass re-audit wave** of the existing in_review backlog. Document the one-time re-audit consequence for legacy items whose `updatedAt` moved after the audit, and its interaction with the pre-flight full-suite cache gate.
7. Dead code cleanup: `_resolve_working_tree_hash` (only used by the fingerprint) is removed; `_resolve_audited_head` stays (still used by green-run attestation).
8. Documentation updated: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (freshness-gate section ~line 134), `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (~line 95), and the code docstrings on `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint` / `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`. Full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics unchanged:** the rule is about *when an existing audit is reused*, never about what the audit concludes. `--force` still bypasses the gate.
- **Read-only:** the fingerprint change must not execute the test suite or make any pi calls.
- **No regression in the freshness skip:** items whose data is unchanged still short-circuit in seconds (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT intent preserved).
- **Fail-open preserved:** any failure to compute the new fingerprint still falls through to a full re-audit (existing behavior).
- **Child reuse gate:** child-audit reuse (LP-0MSQ32MF200675AR, lines ~3877/6056/6391) uses the same fingerprint — it must keep working with the simplified formula (children's own data unchanged → reused).

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`:
  - `_compute_content_fingerprint` (line ~1034) — payload = `{head_sha, description_hash, key_files, working_tree_hash}`.
  - `_check_audit_freshness` (line ~913) — content gate primary; time gate floor for fingerprint-less legacy reports.
  - `_resolve_working_tree_hash` (line ~1080) — only used by the fingerprint (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ).
  - `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX = "Audit content fingerprint: "` (line 431); embedded at lines ~3256/3281/3538.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — fingerprint tests at ~7791-7913 (HEAD sha, description, key files, working-tree states), freshness-gate tests (~2252, 3798-3813, 4275).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness gate behavior section (line ~134).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness gate summary (line ~95).
- Related (separate repo, out of scope): herdr downtime worker's dispatcher-side `isAuditFresh` (ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`, time-based `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`) caused the re-dispatch that exposed this; covered by RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT (ContextHub worklog).

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_compute_content_fingerprint` (simplify), `_check_audit_freshness` (versioned-line handling), `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`, remove `_resolve_working_tree_hash`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — update fingerprint/freshness tests (~7791-7913, 2252, 3798-3813, 4275)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate section
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness-gate summary line

## Related work

- `SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ` — Include working-tree state in the audit content fingerprint (in_review) — the working-tree component this item REMOVES (this item supersedes that component).
- `SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT` — Audit: content-based freshness gate (done) — introduced the fingerprint; this item simplifies its scope.
- `SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0` — Audit runner: detect proxy 'cheap' mode (in_review) — the item whose blocked re-audit exposed this problem.
- `WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT` — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (ContextHub worklog) — dispatcher-side re-dispatch trigger; separate concern.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "this work item's data":** title + description (ACs + Key Files section). Comments, lifecycle fields, and repo state are NOT audited content and must not invalidate.
- **Assumption — migration via versioned line:** legacy v1 reports fall back to the time gate (existing floor for fingerprint-less reports). A legacy item whose `updatedAt` moved after its audit is re-audited once, then stores a v2 fingerprint and is immune to comment/HEAD churn thereafter. Accepted: this is a one-time, bounded transition.
- **Risk — stale code evidence:** dropping the git components means a stored audit may reference code that changed under it (e.g. another work item edits a Key File). Accepted by design per this item's rule; the audit's verdict remains the record for the item's own data.
- **Risk — herdr re-dispatch noise:** herdr may still dispatch /skill:audit for items whose `updatedAt` moved; with this fix the runner short-circuits ("Skipping: audit still fresh", zero pi calls). Dispatcher-side change is out of scope (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should a git HEAD move from another work item invalidate this item's audit? — Answer (user): No. "An audit is only invalidated if there is a change to this work item's data AFTER the audit was created." The rule is that simple.
- Q: What about the working-tree component (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ)? — Answer: remove it too — same reasoning (repo state, not item data). This item supersedes SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ's component.
- Q: Do comments / status / stage changes invalidate? — Answer (assumed, per rule): no — they are not this item's audited data. Document as an explicit decision.
- Q: Migration of existing stored fingerprints? — Answer (assumed): version the fingerprint line so legacy reports are distinguishable; legacy → existing time-gate floor; no mass re-audit wave.
data.title: Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change

## Goal

Prevent the audit runner's Phase-1 code-quality scan from passing non-Python files (YAML, JSON, Markdown, etc.) to ruff as explicit file arguments, eliminating false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings that get auto-created as work items.

## Background / Root cause

On 2026-08-11, an implement self-review audit ran `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files)` with the git changed-file list, which included `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` (uncommitted changes at the time). `_run_ruff_check` invoked `ruff check <yaml-file>` — ruff parses YAML as Python and emitted 121 false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings, which `create_epics_for_findings` auto-created as work items under the Quality Improvement epic (LP-0MSJFTRUW0076Z5Y). Those stale items were later marked completed/in_review and drained one-by-one by the herdr downtime audit tier (~59 dispatches in one evening).

The `.ruff.toml` `exclude = ["*.yaml", "*.yml"]` fix (commit 7580063) is **insufficient**: ruff only honors `exclude` for directory scans; explicit file arguments bypass it (verified: `ruff check config-cheap.yaml` with the exclude in place still returns invalid-syntax findings, while `ruff check .` returns `[]`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `run_ruff` / `_run_ruff_check` filter the `files` list to Python extensions (`.py`, `.pyi`, `.ipynb`) before invoking ruff; non-Python files are skipped and never passed as explicit paths.
2. A regression test asserts ruff is never invoked with a `.yaml`/`.yml` file path when the changed-file list includes one, and that no finding work items are created for non-Python files.
3. Directory-scan behavior (`files=None`) is unchanged.
4. Genuine ruff findings on `.py` files are unaffected (existing tests pass).
data.title: Audit runner: filter non-Python files before passing to ruff

# Audit wall-clock reduction: diagnose and fix why audits take hours

## Problem statement

Item-level audits routinely take hours (measured: 4.25h for a 10-child parent) and
even single-item audits exceed 30 minutes, to the point where operators avoid
running them and release gates stall. Instrumented data from every audit log on
this host shows the cost is not one slow operation but a **long chain of slow,
serial LLM calls against a 2-slot local proxy, oversubscribed by a concurrency
ceiling of 6**, with roughly **18% of total call time producing no usable result**
(timeouts and JSON re-asks).

## Users

- **Release producer** — blocked at the `ship` audit gate, waiting hours for a re-audit.
- **Implementation agent** — cannot complete the implement skill's self-review audit within a session budget.
- **Operator** — avoids auditing, so `in_review` items accumulate unreviewed.

Example user stories:

- As a release producer, I want a single-item audit to finish in **≤ 10 minutes** on a healthy proxy so the `dev`→`main` gate is not a multi-hour stall.
- As an implementation agent, I want a parent audit with 10 children to finish in **≤ 30 minutes** so it fits one session and aborts less often.
- As an operator, I want a **reproducible measurement** of audit wall-clock so I can verify a change actually helped instead of guessing.

## Diagnosis — why audits are slow (measured)

Source: `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/*/*.log`
(465 logs, 491 distinct work items, **1,637 instrumented LLM calls, 140.8h total**).
Reproduce with the script specified in AC1.

### Call-time distribution by phase

| Context | calls | total | p50 | p90 | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `parent` (Phase 1 parent screen) | 450 | **48.3h** | 220s | 954s | 2,705s |
| `child` (Phase 1 child screen) | 412 | **38.1h** | 227s | 633s | 1,572s |
| `verdict_reask` (JSON-contract retry) | 121 | **18.7h** | 461s | 1,466s | 2,372s |
| `phase2_deep` | 285 | 16.0h | 102s | 513s | 1,800s |
| `phase2_child` | 316 | 15.8h | 101s | 529s | 1,775s |
| `false-positive-screen` | 53 | 3.9h | 168s | 600s | 1,200s |

Median call **158s**; 76% of calls ≥ 60s; 35% ≥ 300s.

### Root causes, ranked by measured cost

1. **Phase 1 screening is 62% of all call time (86.4h).** It runs as parent
   screen → N child screens, each a fresh full-prompt session, and averages
   220–227s per call for what is structurally *screening*, not deep analysis.
2. **Concurrency ceiling (6) is 3× the proxy's real capacity (2 slots).**
   `GET /llama/local/status` reports `total_slots: 2`, `available_slots: 0`.
   Six concurrent `pi` sessions queue behind two slots; the queue wait is
   charged against each call's own timeout budget, inflating p90 latency.
3. **~25h of pure timeout waste.** Calls landing exactly on a budget:
   **96 at 600s** (child-screen budget), **13 at 1,800s**, **86 at 90s**.
   Each returns a `partial` fallback that does no work and forces a later re-run.
4. **18.7h of JSON-contract re-asks.** 121 `verdict_reask` calls exist only
   because the first response was not parseable JSON — and the re-ask itself
   has p50 461s, *slower* than the call it retries.
5. **No reuse across the pipeline.** Every phase re-sends its own large prompt;
   a single edited description or touched file invalidates the content
   fingerprint and discards all prior screening work.

### Where the levers are

| Lever | Measured/expected saving | Status in code |
|---|---|---|
| Size concurrency to real slot capacity | removes queue-induced inflation + most 600s/1,800s timeout waste | ceiling hardcoded default 6 (`process_semaphore.py`); slot-status query exists but only used for *child* ceiling |
| Eliminate JSON re-asks | up to 18.7h of 140.8h | `_reask_json_array_once` exists as the fallback; parse robustness not hardened |
| Batch Phase 1 parent+children into one call | collapses N+1 screens to ~1 | `--batch-phase2` exists for Phase 2 only, off by default |
| Route Phase 1 to a fast model | Phase 1 is 62% of time, low-reasoning work | `phase1_model` plumbing exists but **no CLI/env surface**; tiered-model item was demoted |
| Adaptive timeout + degrade early | converts 25h of dead time into fast partials | fixed 600s/1,800s budgets |

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Reproducible measurement harness committed.** A script (e.g. `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py`) parses `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/` and prints the per-context table above (calls, total, p50, p90, max, and count-at-budget). Running it on this host reproduces the baseline numbers in this brief within expected variance, and it is covered by a unit test with a fixture corpus.
- **Baseline is recorded and a target is set.** The measured baseline (1,637 calls / 140.8h / 62% Phase 1 / 18% wasted) is committed to `docs/dev/` and a small-item audit wall-clock target of **≤ 10 minutes** (healthy proxy, no concurrent audits) is stated and used as the regression gate.
- **Concurrency ceiling is sized to real capacity.** The audit runner derives its parallel-call ceiling from the live slot status (`available_slots` / `total_slots`) with a safe floor, never exceeding that capacity, and falls back to the static ceiling when the query fails. Unit tests prove: 2-slot proxy ⇒ ceiling ≤ 2; failed query ⇒ configured fallback; explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` remains authoritative.
- **JSON-contract re-asks are substantially eliminated.** Parse robustness is hardened (strict schema instruction, tolerant extraction, single retry only on genuine failures) and a regression test proves a well-formed model response is never re-asked. Measured `verdict_reask` count drops to ≤ 2% of calls in a re-measurement on the same corpus.
- **Phase 1 call count is reduced.** Parent + child Phase 1 screening is batched and/or routed to a faster model so a 10-child parent issues materially fewer serial Phase 1 calls; a test proves the call count for a 10-child parent is reduced versus the current N+1 structure, with no change to `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` verdict semantics or the ready-to-close gate.
- **Post-change measurement demonstrates the reduction.** Re-running the AC1 harness after implementation shows overall audit LLM wall-clock reduced by **≥ 50%** on a representative audit, with no increase in `partial`-fallback rate and no relaxation of any closure criterion.
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, the audit skill reference, and `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` (or a superseding report).
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics are frozen:** no change may relax the ready-to-close gate;
  a `partial` fallback must never degrade to `met`. Correctness outranks speed.
- **Do not simply raise timeouts.** The historical 900→1200→1800s bumps masked
  the inefficiency; this work reduces actual work, not the ceiling.
- Only **2 local proxy slots** exist — any parallel design must be safe below
  saturation, and must not starve interactive `pi` sessions.
- The runner is a `[READ-ONLY AUDIT]` except the already-documented persistence,
  lifecycle, and ruff-remediation exceptions — no new state mutations.
- Changes land on `dev` only; full suite must be green at the push gate.

## Existing state

- Prior epics `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` (Phase 2 perf, P1–P6) and P7
  (`SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD`) are **complete** and moved the bottleneck from Phase 2
  to Phase 1; that is now confirmed by measurement (§Diagnosis).
- Existing reports: `docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md`.
- Existing levers already in code but not effective by default: `--batch-phase2`,
  `phase1_model` plumbing, child-verdict reuse, content fingerprint gate,
  per-phase checkpoints.
- Related open items: `SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0` (simplify audit freshness) and
  `SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE` (queue/concurrency tuning, done but ceiling remains 6).

## Desired change

A measurable, repeatable audit performance programme: (1) lock in the harness and
baseline, (2) size concurrency to real slot capacity, (3) eliminate JSON re-asks,
(4) collapse Phase 1 call count via batching and/or a fast Phase 1 model, and
(5) re-measure to prove ≥ 50% wall-clock reduction — decomposed into child work
items during the plan stage.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Phase 1 screening, `_call_pi`, timeout
  and parallelism resolution, `_reask_json_array_once`, batch-mode gates.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — concurrency ceiling default (6).
- `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` — slot-status query reused for the ceiling.
- `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` — new measurement harness (AC1).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` — ceiling-from-slots tests.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` — re-ask elimination tests.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` — Phase 1 call-count tests.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` — documentation.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S` — **Audit skill: reduce audit wall-clock time (audits far too slow)** (completed). This is the closest prior attempt and shares the same problem statement. It delivered the content freshness gate, gated child cascade, and scoped code-quality scan — **partial overlap**. This item is deliberately scoped to the *residual* drivers those levers did not remove (Phase 1 = 62% of call time, concurrency ceiling 6 vs 2 real slots, JSON re-asks, ~25h of timeout waste), plus the measurement harness needed to prove any future change is real. It does not re-do the freshness/cascade/scoping work.
- `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` — Audit skill Phase 2 performance evaluation and improvement (complete).
- `SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD` — Phase 1 performance treatment (P7) (complete).
- `SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE` — audit queue timeout / concurrency ceiling tuning (complete; ceiling still 6).
- `SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0` — simplify audit freshness invalidation (open).
- `SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL` — audit reliability RCA (reliability, not latency).
- Docs: `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched `audit`, `speed up`, `Phase 2`, and all prior Phase 1/2 performance items.
One partial overlap found (`SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S`, completed) — its delivered ACs
(freshness gate, child-cascade opt-in, scoped code-quality scan) are **not** the
same as this item's ACs, and re-measurement shows the problem persists. Scope
rewritten to the residual gaps only; recorded above under Related work. One
accidental duplicate created during this intake (`SA-0MVF1GHVX008Q66T`) was
closed as a duplicate of this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the logged `Per-call timing` corpus is representative; it is
  derived from this host's real audit history (491 items) and is the only
  latency evidence available.
- **Risk (quality):** batching Phase 1 into fewer, larger calls could reduce
  verdict quality — mitigated by keeping per-AC verdict semantics and comparing
  verdict output before/after on a fixed item set.
- **Risk (contention):** a parallel design sized to slots could still contend
  with interactive sessions — mitigated by a floor of 1 and never exceeding
  `available_slots`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** adjacency to freshness simplification
  (`SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0`) and the merge-gate work — those stay separate items;
  this epic links rather than absorbs them.
- **Risk (measurement):** historical numbers were taken under concurrent audit
  load; targets must be re-measured clean-room for a fair comparison.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Is the complaint about *all* audits or a specific class (single-item vs
  multi-child parent)?
  **Answer (operator, seed prompt):** "Audits take far too long" — general.
  Diagnosis shows both are affected: single-item ~10–30 min, 10-child parent
  4.25h. Scope therefore covers both, with the parent case as the primary target.
  Source: seed prompt `/intake` request; evidence: per-context table above.

- **Q:** Should the fix raise timeouts or reduce actual work?
  **Answer (derived from prior art):** Reduce actual work. Prior bumps
  (900→1200→1800s) are documented as masking inefficiency
  (`docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md` §1). Source: repo docs.

- **Q:** Is switching off the local proxy (to a remote model) acceptable?
  **Answer (OPEN QUESTION — producer decision):** assumed *permitted but not
  required*; the plan prefers fast/local routing and treats remote routing
  (e.g. `deepseek-v4-flash`) as an option to confirm. Source: this intake;
  needs producer confirmation at plan review.
data.title: Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

# Right-size `AUDIT_CHILD_SCREEN_TIMEOUT` and quarantine capped-screen verdicts

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG (audit wall-clock reduction)
**Discovered-from:** WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B (ContextHub) · **RCA:** `docs/dev/audit-child-demotion-rca.md`

## Problem statement

Child Phase-1 AC screens run on a fixed `_CHILD_SCREEN_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT = 600` s budget (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` ~L631-642, env `AUDIT_CHILD_SCREEN_TIMEOUT`). On a loaded reference host that budget is **marginal, not generous**: in the 2026-10-21 ContextHub run, **5 of 11** child screens landed exactly on the cap (600.03–600.12 s) and 6 completed in 336–506 s. The capped screens then burn a further `verdict_reask` (2 more calls hit 600 s) and finally fall back to `partial` diagnostics.

Consequences beyond lost wall-clock (the parent epic's concern):

- **Tainted verdicts.** `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY calls=27 parse_ok=20 parse_failed=7 timeouts=7` — 26 % of calls produced no usable verdict, and 8 of 11 children were persisted as `Ready to close: No` on that tainted evidence.
- **Wrong lifecycle outcomes.** Those tainted 'No's were then persisted through `wl audit-set`, whose `revertToPlanComplete` side effect demoted all 11 `in_review` children (see the sibling bug item for that defect). Right-sizing the budget removes the main *source* of tainted child verdicts.
- **Selection bias.** Children whose FILE SCOPE is small (docs/XS items) complete comfortably; children with 6–7 ACs and wide manifests cap out, so the ones most likely to need judgement are the ones that lose it.

## Measured data (2026-10-21, ContextHub, 16-core host, load ~3)

| child screen | elapsed (s) |
|---|---:|
| F1 `WL-0MVFRR98A008MM19` | **600.12** (capped) |
| F2 `WL-0MVFRRAXD001E7AN` | 336.41 |
| F3 `WL-0MVFRRCP7007UWS7` | **600.11** (capped) |
| F5 `WL-0MVFRREMZ0085G7I` | **600.05** (capped) |
| F8 `WL-0MVFRRGGC001IQK1` | 506.12 |
| F4 `WL-0MVFRRKKN00544PQ` | 337.44 |
| F6 `WL-0MVFRRMX3003UPP3` | 258.12 |
| F7 `WL-0MVFRROLM002K98B` | 463.25 |
| F9 `WL-0MVFRRQ9W003KEFL` | **600.03** (capped) |
| F10 `WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J` | **600.05** (capped) |
| F11 `WL-0MVFRRTY5001KTNH` | 394.36 |

Completed-screen distribution: min 258 s, median 389 s, max 506 s — i.e. the **unconstrained** p95 is already ≈506 s, leaving ~15 % headroom against a 600 s cap. Any host-load increase converts completions into timeouts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The child-screen budget is derived from measured data rather than a hard-coded constant: p95 of completed child screens across the recorded corpus, multiplied by a documented safety factor (proposal: ≥ 2× — this host's completed p95 is 506 s, implying ≈1,000–1,200 s), with the derivation recorded in a comment/docstring and the constant updated.
- The chosen value is validated against the corpus: re-running the measurement shows ≤ 5 % of child screens landing on the cap (currently 45 %), with the measurement command documented.
- A capped child screen is never reported as a plain `partial` indistinguishable from a model judgement: its evidence names the timeout and the phase, and the run's `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY` surfaces `child_screen_timeouts=N` so downstream consumers can quarantine it.
- The interaction with the parent-process budget is checked: raising the child-screen cap must not make the parent `--parent-timeout` (110 s + 600 s/child) the new starvation point; adjust that scaling formula in the same change if needed, and note the trade-off.
- FILE SCOPE and AC-count correlation is recorded (children capping out had 6–7 ACs and wide manifests) so a future manifest-width bound can be evaluated.
- `skill/audit/tests/` passes.

## Out of scope

Reducing the *number* or *cost* of child Phase 1 calls (parent epic AC5) and concurrency sizing (parent epic AC3) — this item only fixes the budget itself and the observability of a capped screen.
## Parent AC traceability

- **AC2 (parent)** — the derived child-screen budget is validated against the corpus using
  the measurement harness from parent AC1 (the sibling harness child), satisfying the
  "validated against the corpus ... measurement command documented" requirement.
- **AC4 (parent)** — capped screens are no longer indistinguishable `partial` fallbacks and
  are counted in `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY`, directly reducing the wasted-call share that
  parent AC4 measures.
- Out of scope for the parent epic's AC3 (concurrency ceiling) and AC5 (Phase 1 call
  count) — owned by sibling children.

# Audit performance measurement harness and committed baseline

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As an operator or release producer, I want a committed, reproducible measurement of
audit LLM call timing, so I can verify that a performance change actually helped
instead of guessing.

## Problem statement

Every audit log on this host contains `Per-call timing:` lines, but no committed tool
parses them. The parent brief's baseline (1,637 instrumented calls, 140.8 h total,
62 % of call time in Phase 1, ~18 % wasted on timeouts and JSON re-asks) was produced
ad hoc and cannot be reproduced or regression-gated.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (parent):** `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` is committed. It parses `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/` (configurable root) and prints the per-context table with columns: context, calls, total, p50, p90, max, and count-at-budget. Running it on this host reproduces the parent brief's baseline figures within expected variance (documented tolerance).
- **AC1 (parent):** The harness is covered by a unit test using a small fixture corpus of synthetic debug logs — the test is written before the parser logic (TDD) and asserts each aggregate column including the count-at-budget buckets (600 s, 900 s, 1,800 s).
- **AC2 (parent):** `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` records the measured baseline (calls, total hours, per-context breakdown, Phase 1 share, wasted share) together with the reproduction command and a stated single-item audit wall-clock target of **≤ 10 minutes** on a healthy proxy with no concurrent audits, which becomes the regression gate.
- **AC2 (parent):** The baseline document names the gate explicitly and is referenced from `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.
- The harness is read-only: it never writes to `~/.audit_debug/`, `.worklog/`, or the audit runner.
- UK English throughout.
- **Parent AC1 traceability:** a script `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` parses `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/` and prints the per-context table (calls, total, p50, p90, max, count-at-budget); running it on this host reproduces the baseline in this brief within expected variance; it is covered by a unit test with a fixture corpus.
- **Parent AC2 traceability:** the measured baseline (1,637 calls / 140.8h / 62% Phase 1 / 18% wasted) is committed to `docs/dev/` and a small-item audit wall-clock target of **≤ 10 minutes** (healthy proxy, no concurrent audits) is stated and used as the regression gate.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Write `scripts/tests/test_measure_audit_performance.py` against a fixture corpus
   (5–8 synthetic logs spanning each context) — asserts table shape and aggregates.
2. Implement `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` with `--root`, `--context`,
   `--at-budget` CLI options and stable table output.
3. Run it on this host; record the output in `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md`
   with the mandated ≤ 10 min target and reproduction command.
4. Link the baseline doc from `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` — new harness
- `scripts/tests/test_measure_audit_performance.py` — new unit tests + fixture logs
- `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` — new baseline + target document
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — link to the baseline document

## Dependencies

None — this is the foundation slice; every other child depends on it.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the recorded `~/.audit_debug` corpus is representative (491 items,
  one host). The document records the host, date range and per-context counts so a
  different corpus is obviously different.
- **Risk:** debug logs may be pruned during the work; the fixture corpus makes the unit
  test independent of live logs while the baseline document pins the snapshot.
data.title: Audit performance measurement harness and baseline

# Size audit concurrency ceiling to real proxy slot capacity

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As an implementation agent or release producer, I want the audit runner's parallel-call
ceiling to match the proxy's real slot capacity, so calls do not queue behind slots and
inflate their own timeout budget into avoidable 600 s / 1,800 s caps.

## Problem statement

`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` defaults to 6 (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`) while
`GET /llama/local/status` reports `total_slots: 2`, `available_slots: 0`. Six concurrent
`pi` sessions queue behind two slots; queue wait is charged against each call's timeout,
inflating p90 and pushing calls onto their budget (96 calls at 600 s, 13 at 1,800 s).
Slot-status querying already exists (`skill/audit/scripts/scan.py`) but is only used for
the *child* ceiling.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC3 (parent):** The audit runner derives its parallel-call ceiling from live slot status (`available_slots` / `total_slots`) with a safe floor of 1, never exceeding reported capacity.
- **AC3 (parent):** When the slot query fails or times out, the runner falls back to the configured static ceiling (current behaviour preserved).
- **AC3 (parent):** An explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` value remains authoritative — it is never silently overridden by slot discovery.
- **AC3 (parent):** Unit tests prove all three behaviours: 2-slot proxy ⇒ ceiling ≤ 2; failed query ⇒ configured fallback; explicit env var ⇒ that exact value.
- The ceiling derivation is logged once per run (slot status, derived ceiling, source) so the decision is observable in the audit log.
- Full `skill/audit/tests/` suite passes.
- **Parent AC3 traceability:** the audit runner derives its parallel-call ceiling from the live slot status (`available_slots` / `total_slots`) with a safe floor, never exceeding that capacity, falling back to the static ceiling when the query fails; unit tests prove 2-slot proxy ⇒ ceiling ≤ 2; failed query ⇒ configured fallback; explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` remains authoritative.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Write the failing concurrency tests first in
   `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` (mock slot status).
2. Add a `_resolve_audit_ceiling()` helper in `audit_runner.py` that queries slot status
   (reusing the existing `scan.py` query), clamps by floor 1 and `total_slots`, and
   honours an explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`.
3. Route every ceiling consumer through the helper (parent and child paths).
4. Log the derivation once per run; update the constant docstring in
   `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` to describe the derivation rather than a bare 6.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — ceiling resolution and consumers
- `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` — existing slot-status query to reuse
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — ceiling default documentation
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` — new tests
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — ceiling behaviour section

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the measurement harness + baseline child (SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG child 1):
  the change must be measured before/after with the committed harness.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (contention):** a slot-derived ceiling could still contend with interactive
  sessions. Mitigated by the floor of 1 and never exceeding `available_slots`.
- **Assumption:** `available_slots` is a trustworthy signal for admission; the fallback
  path keeps the runner functional when it is not.
- **Constraint:** do not raise timeouts to compensate — this change reduces queueing,
  not the budget.
data.title: Size audit concurrency ceiling to real proxy slot capacity

# Eliminate JSON-contract re-asks

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As an implementation agent, I want a well-formed model response to be accepted on the
first call, so audit wall-clock is not spent re-asking — and the re-ask itself (p50
461 s, slower than the call it retries) is not billed twice.

## Problem statement

121 `verdict_reask` calls cost 18.7 h (13 % of all measured call time) and exist only
because the first response was not parseable JSON. `_reask_json_array_once` is the
fallback path; parse robustness is not hardened, so genuine-but-unusual formatting
(fenced blocks, prose prefix, trailing commas) triggers a full second call.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC4 (parent):** Parse robustness is hardened — a strict schema instruction is added to the prompt, tolerant extraction handles fenced ```json blocks and prose-prefixed JSON, and a single retry is attempted **only** on genuine failures (no parseable array found, or failed schema validation).
- **AC4 (parent):** A regression test proves a well-formed model response is never re-asked (the retry path is not invoked when the first response parses).
- **AC4 (parent):** Additional regression tests cover fenced blocks, prose-prefixed JSON, and trailing-comma tolerance — each accepted without a re-ask.
- **AC4 (parent):** A re-measurement on the same corpus shows `verdict_reask` at ≤ 2 % of all calls (currently ~7.4 %), recorded in the baseline document's successor report.
- Verdict semantics are unchanged: no response that would previously have been re-asked and then rejected may now be silently accepted with different semantics; the `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` vocabulary and the ready-to-close gate are frozen.
- Full `skill/audit/tests/` suite passes.
- **Parent AC4 traceability:** parse robustness is hardened (strict schema instruction, tolerant extraction, single retry only on genuine failures) and a regression test proves a well-formed model response is never re-asked; measured `verdict_reask` count drops to ≤ 2% of calls in a re-measurement on the same corpus.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Write the failing tests first in
   `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py`: well-formed ⇒ no re-ask;
   fenced ⇒ parsed; prose-prefixed ⇒ parsed; trailing comma ⇒ parsed; genuinely
   unparseable ⇒ exactly one re-ask.
2. Harden `_extract_json_array` (tolerant extraction) and add an explicit JSON-schema
   instruction to the Phase 1 prompt template.
3. Gate `_reask_json_array_once` on genuine failure only; count re-asks in the
   `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY`.
4. Re-run the measurement harness and record the re-ask share.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — prompt template, `_extract_json_array`,
  `_reask_json_array_once`, reliability summary
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` — new tests
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — JSON contract section
- `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` — re-measurement record

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the measurement harness + baseline child (child 1) — the ≤ 2 % claim must
  be measured with the committed harness.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (correctness):** tolerant parsing could accept malformed verdicts. Mitigated by
  schema validation after extraction and by keeping the retry for genuine failures.
- **Constraint:** verdict semantics are frozen (parent brief §Constraints).
data.title: Eliminate JSON-contract re-asks

# Reduce Phase 1 screening call count

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As a release producer, I want a 10-child parent audit to issue materially fewer serial
Phase 1 calls, so the dominant 62 % cost centre stops dominating wall-clock.

## Problem statement

Phase 1 runs as one parent screen plus N child screens, each a fresh full-prompt session
averaging 220–227 s — 86.4 h of the measured 140.8 h. `--batch-phase2` exists for Phase 2
only and is off by default; `phase1_model` plumbing exists but has no CLI/env surface.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC5 (parent):** Parent and child Phase 1 screening is batched and/or routed to a faster model so a 10-child parent issues materially fewer serial Phase 1 calls than the current N+1 structure.
- **AC5 (parent):** A test proves the Phase 1 call count for a 10-child parent is reduced versus the current N+1 structure (asserted against a fake `_call_pi` call counter).
- **AC5 (parent):** A CLI/env surface exists for the Phase 1 model (`--phase1-model` / `AUDIT_PHASE1_MODEL`), defaulting to current behaviour so no existing invocation changes model silently.
- **AC5 (parent):** There is **no change** to `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` verdict semantics or to the ready-to-close gate; a batching on/off comparison on a fixed item set is recorded showing equivalent verdicts.
- Full `skill/audit/tests/` suite passes.
- **Parent AC5 traceability:** parent + child Phase 1 screening is batched and/or routed to a faster model so a 10-child parent issues materially fewer serial Phase 1 calls; a test proves the call count is reduced versus the current N+1 structure, with no change to `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` verdict semantics or the ready-to-close gate.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Write the failing call-count test first
   (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py`): a 10-child parent under batching
   issues fewer `_call_pi` invocations than the N+1 baseline, and verdicts are unchanged.
2. Extend the existing `--batch-phase2` flag family with `--batch-phase1` (default
   preserving current behaviour until the comparison evidence exists), reusing the
   Phase 2 batching machinery.
3. Expose `--phase1-model` / `AUDIT_PHASE1_MODEL` on the existing `phase1_model` plumbing.
4. Record a fixed-item-set verdict comparison and the call-count delta.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Phase 1 screening, batch gates, model selection
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` — new call-count and parity tests
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — new flags
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — Phase 1 batching and model routing

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the measurement harness + baseline child (child 1).
- Independent of the concurrency-ceiling and JSON-re-ask children, but should land after
  them so the remaining Phase 1 cost is measured on an un-inflated baseline.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (quality):** batching into fewer, larger calls could reduce verdict quality —
  mitigated by the fixed-item-set parity comparison and keeping per-AC verdicts.
- **Risk (default change):** enabling batching by default without parity evidence would
  violate the frozen-semantics constraint; the flag therefore defaults to current
  behaviour until the comparison is recorded.
- **Assumption:** a fast Phase 1 model is permissible; the remote-model option remains an
  OPEN QUESTION for the producer (parent brief Appendix) and is not required by this item.
data.title: Reduce Phase 1 screening call count

# Post-change measurement: verify ≥ 50 % wall-clock reduction

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As a release producer, I want a post-change measurement proving the audit wall-clock
reduction is real, so the epic closes on evidence rather than assertion.

## Problem statement

Individual levers each claim savings; nothing proves the combined effect, and the parent
brief requires ≥ 50 % reduction with no increase in `partial`-fallback rate and no
relaxation of any closure criterion.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC6 (parent):** Re-running the AC1 harness after all code children land shows overall audit LLM wall-clock reduced by **≥ 50 %** on a representative audit, measured clean-room (no concurrent audits) and compared against the committed baseline.
- **AC6 (parent):** The `partial`-fallback rate has not increased versus the baseline.
- **AC6 (parent):** Every closure criterion is unchanged — the report states explicitly that no ready-to-close rule was relaxed, with the diff (none) shown.
- A single-item audit completes within the ≤ 10 minute target on a healthy proxy.
- The result is recorded in `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` (or a superseding report) as a before/after table with reproduction commands.
- **Parent AC6 traceability:** re-running the measurement harness after implementation shows overall audit LLM wall-clock reduced by **≥ 50%** on a representative audit, with no increase in `partial`-fallback rate and no relaxation of any closure criterion.
- **Parent AC8 traceability:** the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Run the committed harness against the same corpus and against a live clean-room
   single-item audit and a 10-child parent audit.
2. Produce the before/after table (calls, total hours, p50, p90, Phase 1 share, re-ask
   share, timeout share, partial rate).
3. Assess against the three gates (≥ 50 %, partial rate not increased, closure criteria
   unchanged); if a gate fails, record the shortfall and open a follow-up child rather
   than weakening the gate.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` — post-change section
- `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` — reused unchanged
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — no change expected (verification only)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by every code child: measurement harness, concurrency ceiling, JSON re-asks,
  Phase 1 call count, and the child-screen budget right-sizing item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (measurement):** historical numbers were taken under concurrent load; the
  comparison must be clean-room, and the report states the host and load conditions.
- **Risk (shortfall):** if ≥ 50 % is not met, do not relax the gate — record the shortfall
  and open a follow-up.

## Parent AC traceability

- **AC6 (parent):** covered above (≥ 50 % reduction, partial rate, closure criteria).
- **AC8 (parent):** this verification child runs the full project test suite (unit,
  integration, and skill tests) as a final regression gate and records the result —
  the last child before documentation, so a red tree is caught here.
data.title: Post-change measurement: verify 50% wall-clock reduction

# Update audit performance documentation

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer or agent, I want the audit skill documentation to describe the new
ceiling derivation, batching flags, JSON contract and measured performance, so the
behaviour is discoverable and the numbers are traceable.

## Problem statement

The parent brief's AC7 requires all related documentation to reflect the changes — the
audit skill doc, the audit skill reference, code comments, and the measured report. The
code children update fragments; this item guarantees no stale claim remains.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC7 (parent):** `skill/audit/SKILL.md` documents the new Phase 1 flags (`--batch-phase1`, `--phase1-model`) and the slot-derived concurrency ceiling.
- **AC7 (parent):** `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` documents the ceiling derivation (floor, fallback, `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` precedence), the JSON-contract hardening, and links the baseline/after report.
- **AC7 (parent):** `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` is updated or explicitly superseded by the new measured report.
- **AC7 (parent):** Code comments and docstrings reflect the changes — no comment still claims a fixed ceiling of 6 or an uncalibrated 600 s child-screen budget.
- A documentation sweep (grep) confirms no stale reference to the old defaults remains, with the search commands and results recorded in the work item.
- UK English throughout.
- **Parent AC7 traceability:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, the audit skill reference, and `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` (or a superseding report).

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Grep for stale values: `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, `600`, `phase1_model`,
   `batch-phase2`, `verdict_reask` across `skill/`, `docs/dev/`, `scripts/`.
2. Update each hit to the new behaviour and cross-link the baseline/after report.
3. Record the sweep commands and results in the work item comment.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`
- `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` (or superseding report)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — comments/docstrings only
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — comments/docstrings only

## Dependencies

- Blocked by every code child and by the post-change measurement child (the docs must
  state the measured result, not a projection).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Constraint:** do not edit `CHANGELOG.md` (managed by the ship skill's release
  pipeline).
- **Constraint:** documentation-only changes must not alter behaviour.
